claude_proposed_widenings.name: DurationEndTrigger.target_study_check_success
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Maze's concentration ends early when the banished target succeeds on a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check via the Study action. No existing DurationEndTrigger variant captures a target ability-check success as an early-end condition. The closest existing variants (target_makes_attack_roll, target_casts_spell, etc.) are all output-based actions, not resolution outcomes.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The target can take a Study action to try to escape. When it does so, it makes a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check. If it succeeds, it escapes, and the spell ends.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: transport_exile returnOnSpellEnd field
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: When Maze ends by any means, the exiled target reappears at its original departure point (or nearest unoccupied space). The transport_exile atom encodes only the outbound banishment; there is no field to encode the return destination semantics. This is a distinct need from teleport (which is caster-initiated repositioning) — here the return is automatic on duration expiry.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When the spell ends, the target reappears in the space it left or, if that space is occupied, in the nearest unoccupied space.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ability_check_gate skillFilter (OngoingEffect variant)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Maze's escape check is specifically Intelligence (Investigation), not just any Intelligence check. The OngoingEffect ability_check_gate type exposes only `ability: Ability` with no skillFilter field, so the Investigation sub-spec cannot be encoded. The ActivationPhase ability_check_gate has the same gap.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: it makes a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check
